characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al aged 1 h: increase in YS, UTS and hardness, and only a minor reduction in TE.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

characterization_methods.key_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al aged 1 h, hardness increases (increasing with aging temperature).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques
characterization_methods.key_findings: No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations; fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure investigation (cracks, pores, macrosegregations, grain size)

interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbides form in the austenitic matrix during aging of Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al.

phase_interfaces.coherence: lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix

processing_steps.method: vacuum-induction melting (VIM) and casting into Cu molds
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five different alloys synthesized in one operation from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast, remaining melt composition adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130 mm³ blocks hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets.
Sheets reheated to 1100 °C and water quenched, then cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into 2×60×55 mm³ segments.
Homogenization performed at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar followed by water quenching.
Aging conducted in air at 450 °C for 1 h followed by oil quenching; this is the sample-defining aging step (one of nine heat treatments per composition).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: tensile specimens prepared from 2×60×55 mm³ segments; cross-sections perpendicular to the rolling direction

phases_present.morphology: nm-sized precipitates (reported to form cuboidal nanoprecipitates in the austenitic matrix)

precipitates.coherency: lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix
precipitates.distribution: formed in the austenitic matrix during aging
precipitates.type: κ-carbide (L'1₂ ordered fcc; non-oxide perovskite; approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC)

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenitic matrix containing nm-sized κ-carbides formed during aging; no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations observed.

unmapped_findings: For Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, aging for 1 h leads to an increase in yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and hardness (increasing with temperature) and only a minor reduction in total elongation; the 450 °C/1 h condition is one of these 1-h aging states (no numeric values for this specific condition are printed in the text).
The pronounced strengthening of the ~8 wt.% Al variant during aging is attributed to the formation of nm-sized κ-carbides.
This sample belongs to the RAP screening matrix of 45 material conditions (Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl with nine heat treatments; 135 tensile tests and hardness measurements in total).
Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al is the alloy with the highest Al content and lowest density among the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-xAl set studied here.

For κ-carbide-strengthened austenitic steels, the prevalent deformation mechanism is suggested to be Orowan bypassing of κ-carbide rods followed by dislocation-loop expansion, assisted by dislocation cross-slip and minor shearing of κ-carbides (discussed for the κ-carbide-strengthened 8Al class, referenced to the 24 h/600 °C example).
